direct_file_reviews.summary: The prompt requires a pure Node.js ESM `.mjs` migration of the Python JWT CLI with manual argv parsing, no npm dependencies, no Python, and output files under `/output`.
The aggregate cell record shows actual parallel use, three subagents, artifact validation success, and a completed official evaluation failing at 49 of 70.
The completed official status resolves the parallel outcome: artifact copy succeeded, parallel protocol validation passed, and `solution_passed` is false with 49/70 samples.
The evaluator summary independently repeats the completed official RepoZero Py2JS result and the 0.7 pass rate for the parallel artifact.
The final answer lists the parent-owned `/output` files and claims verification of visible sample JWTs plus selected CLI edge cases.

timeline_reviews.summary: The main transport stream records the parent probing CLI behavior, writing the `/output` module tree, fixing signer runtime failures, receiving a child result, listing final files, and closing.

The parallel parent session owns the delivered `/output` implementation, spawns `/root/cli_probe`, performs extensive executable probing, replaces the Web Crypto signer with local SHA-256/HMAC, verifies visible cases, waits for the child, and finalizes.

The first child probes CLI behavior, spawns its own nested probe, writes an alternate implementation under `/workspace/output`, verifies visible samples and CLI behavior, and returns a detailed final answer to the parent.
The nested child is a CLI-probing worker: it runs executable edge-case commands, edits no deliverable files, and returns observed argparse behavior.

direct_file_reviews.summary: The serial prompt is byte-identical and requires the same pure Node.js ESM `.mjs` migration, manual command-line parsing, local modules, and `/output` delivery.
The serial aggregate record shows no parallel uptake, no subagents, artifact validation success, and a completed official evaluation failing at 49 of 70.
The completed serial official status resolves the control outcome: protocol validation passes, no child activity is present, and `solution_passed` is false with 49/70 samples.
The evaluator summary repeats the completed official RepoZero Py2JS result and 0.7 pass rate for the serial artifact.
The final answer lists the serial `/output` module hierarchy, includes the entry file excerpt, and claims visible sample and CLI-edge verification.

timeline_reviews.summary: The serial transport stream records one agent probing executable behavior, implementing the module tree under `/output`, verifying visible sample tokens and selected argparse cases, and closing.
The raw serial session confirms a single-agent workflow with no delegation, OpenSSL-backed signing through `node:child_process`, visible token verification, CLI checks, and final delivery.

parallel.requirements: The parallel parent recognized ESM `.mjs` output, manual `process.argv` behavior, exact stdout/stderr parity, zero npm dependencies, and the no-Python/no-`node:crypto` constraints from the prompt.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: The parent kept implementation ownership while delegating CLI probing to `/root/cli_probe`; that child spawned a nested CLI probe and also produced an alternate implementation under `/workspace/output`.
parallel.implementation: The delivered parent implementation used modules for program name, CLI formatting/parsing, base64url, SHA-256, HMAC signature, JWT assembly, and `test1.mjs`; after Web Crypto failed under file execution, it replaced signing with local SHA-256/HMAC code.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: The parent delivered the `/output` tree it created, listing flat library files and `test1.mjs`; the child implementation under `/workspace/output` was not the artifact tree validated by status.
parallel.verification: The parent verified the four visible sample JWTs and a shell parity loop covering several CLI edge cases, then received the child's final result before closing.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: The completed official evaluator still marked the artifact failing at 49/70; the raw record does not expose the individual hidden failures, so the unresolved defect is an ordinary implementation or coverage gap rather than a proven coordination consequence.

serial.requirements: The serial run recognized the same ESM `.mjs`, manual `argparse`-compatible CLI, output formatting, local module, and no npm dependency requirements.
serial.plan_and_ownership: One agent handled probing, implementation, verification, and final response without any child delegation or parallel control violation.
serial.implementation: The serial implementation split CLI parsing/messages/program-name, JWT base64url/json/encoding, an OpenSSL-backed HS256 signer, IO helpers, and the `test1.mjs` entry point under `/output`.
serial.integration_and_delivery: The single owner created the `/output` module tree directly and artifact validation captured the expected `test1.mjs` plus library files.
serial.verification: The serial run verified the visible sample JWT outputs and selected parser edge cases including help precedence, missing payload, abbreviations, empty values, and positional errors.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: The completed official evaluator also marked the serial artifact failing at 49/70; no serial delegation issue exists, and the failed hidden cases are not detailed in the mounted evidence.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel identified JWT output parity, manual argparse-style CLI parsing, ESM `.mjs` files, local modules, `/output` delivery, and no npm/Python/`node:crypto` constraints.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial identified the same prompt requirements and executable-as-oracle workflow.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No material requirement recognition difference is evidenced; both targeted the visible CLI and sample-token surface.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel split off CLI probing to a child and nested child, while the parent retained the implementation and final artifact path.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial used one owner for probing, implementation, testing, and final delivery.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The parallel decomposition added redundant probe/alternate implementation work, but there was still a parent implementation owner and no missing ownership consequence.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The child returned usable CLI observations and an alternate implementation path, but the parent already had its own delivered `/output` path and did not need an inter-agent interface to assemble the artifact.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no child handoff boundary and kept all CLI observations in a single context.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The parallel run had additional handoff surfaces, yet no missing requirement, stale, lossy, or conflicting handoff is tied to the official failure.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel initially tried Web Crypto, observed runtime failures, then implemented local SHA-256/HMAC and JWT modules.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial implemented the same high-level JWT/CLI behavior but used a `node:child_process` OpenSSL signing helper.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The signer implementation differs, but both delivered artifacts reached the same official 49/70 score, so the implementation difference is not an outcome differentiator in this pair.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parent waited for the child, saw timeouts during waits, received the child final result, then listed and finalized the parent-owned `/output` artifact.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no result lifecycle beyond local command outputs and file edits.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The parallel child result arrived before closure but was redundant with parent work; the lack of adoption did not produce a distinct adverse final state relative to serial.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The delivered parallel artifact was the parent's `/output` tree; the child wrote a separate `/workspace/output` tree, and the status artifact list matches the parent's final file list.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial artifact list matches its single-owner `/output` tree and contains the expected entry point plus libraries.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had another workspace tree but no concrete collision or overwrite of the validated deliverable is proven.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel verified four visible token samples and a CLI parity sweep, then official evaluation failed at 49/70.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial verified the same visible token samples and selected CLI cases, then official evaluation also failed at 49/70.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both accepted visible parity without evidence of the hidden failing cases; no parallel-specific verification omission is isolated.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel used more wall time, LLM requests, and three subagents, but it did not time out and closed after its local checks and child-result receipt.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial used fewer requests and no subagents, also without timeout, and closed after local checks.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel was more expensive and redundant, but budget pressure did not displace a known necessary step before closure.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The current completed official evaluation gives both trajectories the same failing result: 49 passed out of 70. The concrete process difference is that parallel delegated and received redundant CLI/alternate-implementation work while serial stayed single-agent and used an OpenSSL-backed signer. Both nonetheless delivered a visible-sample-passing ESM module tree and both failed the hidden official set, so the pair does not support a parallel-side coordination label as an outcome explanation.
parallel_contributors: Parallel delegation produced extra CLI observations and an alternate `/workspace/output` implementation, but the parent finalized its own `/output` implementation.
The parent verified visible samples and selected CLI cases but did not have mounted evidence for the hidden failing cases.
serial_contributors: Serial completed the same visible sample and CLI verification in one context.
Serial used a different signing implementation but reached the same official 49/70 result.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Parallel used pure JavaScript SHA-256/HMAC after Web Crypto runtime failures; serial used an OpenSSL subprocess helper.
Both attempts appear to rely on visible ASCII/sample JWT and CLI probes, while the official failing cases are not individually available in the mounted records.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: no outcome difference; shared ordinary implementation or coverage gap

candidates.reason: The parallel parent explicitly owned and wrote the delivered implementation; child work was auxiliary rather than the only implementation path.
There were not multiple required component implementations needing reconciliation into one final artifact; the parent integrated its own modules.
The parent owned final assembly and placed `test1.mjs` plus libraries under `/output`, as confirmed by final file listing and artifact validation.
The parent drove implementation, verification, final file listing, and closure; the end-to-end pipeline was not ownerless.
The parent probed executable behavior but implementation work was not blocked behind one mandatory serial preflight with a concrete delay consequence.
Investigation and implementation overlapped across parent and children, and no later productive stage was left incomplete because all investigation completed first.
The indispensable implementation path stayed with the parent and completed; auxiliary child work did not starve a known critical correction path.
Although the parallel run used three subagents and more tokens, it did not time out and no required work is shown as displaced by collective fan-out.
The child produced CLI findings and even an alternate implementation; the issue is redundancy, not a demonstrably overbroad child task leaving indispensable work unfinished.
The executed child was asked to probe CLI behavior and returned useful CLI findings; no already-known required fact is shown missing from the brief and causing unusable work.
The final artifact did not depend on interoperating separately owned components from multiple agents, so no missing cross-agent file or API contract caused incompatibility.
No known finding is shown disappearing in transfer; the child returned a detailed final answer and the parent already had equivalent local findings.
The child handoff was detailed but not proven too large for a decision window, and there is no dependent action left unfinished because of handoff volume.
The child's alternate `/workspace/output` path differed from the parent's deliverable, but no parent action consumed stale workspace state and caused rework or invalid verification.
No incompatible returned reports or contracts were left unadjudicated; parent and child both reported visible sample and CLI parity.
The parent did present completion after local checks, but no non-evaluator, parent-visible unresolved integrated mismatch is evidenced before closure.
There is no replacement or retry child repeating previous failed work without inherited findings; the nested child was a probe, not a checkpoint-free retry.
